0.content:
Neuvillette brought the Melusines to the Court of Fontaine and found them work. Sigewinne respects him enormously and calls him "Monsieur Neuvillette". He tried her for breaking the ancient law against turning another species into a human; she accepted willingly and agreed with his verdict. The day she left for the Fortress it rained hard, but she remembers the rain as warm and gentle, like the way he looks at her. They have written to each other ever since: she answers every letter earnestly and adds Fortress anecdotes in case he is bored at the Palais Mermonia, and he sends medical supplies. When it rains she wonders what he is feeling. She praises his water-drinking as a very healthy habit.

Neuvillette told Wriothesley he has always seen himself as a concerned parent to her. He says he would summon Wriothesley at the first rumour of her being bullied, and he looks forward to her vacations; on one she brought him Kamera film and asked to hear more of his commentary on Natlan's water. He personally came out against rumours that she is part-human. After the truth about her teacher came out, he expressed regret at the law's harshness, and confirmed she owes no further punishment.

Asked whom she would save first if he and a human fell into the water, she says he would help her bring the human safely to shore. She told the Traveler that Neuvillette sent her to the Fortress to look after everyone's well-being. She wishes he would visit more often and thinks he would like the Fortress, "with all the darkness and chaos".

1.content:
Sigewinne has served every administrator of the Fortress of Meropide, and Wriothesley is the latest. She met him as a newly arrived boy who had beaten a long-time bully. He refused anaesthetic while she stitched him, so she later slipped it into his tea. She thinks of him as an impressive little grown-up who became an impressive big one. Under Wriothesley she has the Fortress's protection: rudeness to her is punished extra harshly. She calls him "the Duke" or "Your Grace", nags him about drinking too much tea, and keeps trying to get him to drink her milkshakes.

At Neuvillette's request she reported on the boy in her letters for years. When Wriothesley found out, he accused the Iudex of planting a spy and argued that the Iudex cannot show concern. She did not argue, but privately thought him mistaken: she knew Neuvillette had ordered the Melusine officer who once fed the starving young Wriothesley to do it. She then wrote Neuvillette that she had found a secret even the Duke does not know. Wriothesley says she has all the virtues of the medical profession, and admits she picked up a bad habit from him: betting with her Melusine friends over who can stick more stickers on his belongings. He says it does not bother him.

He sends her on vacations she would never take. He approved her joining the Butterfly Dew investigation despite the misgivings of Morgane, the Marechaussee Phantom officer on the case, accompanied her to her teacher's memorial, and in 6.3 took her to Liyue's Lantern Rite to use up her leave (limited event). He jokes that he is her junior colleague, since she has been in the Fortress longer than almost anyone. She once complained he skipped a photo shoot and praised him for using Jurieu and Lourvine as shields from prying eyes.

2.content:
In the days when no human would teach a Melusine, a gruff travelling doctor whom children called "the witch" took Sigewinne on, scared off the children who mocked her, and gave her a medical kit. Sigewinne called her "Teacher" (sometimes "Master"). The witch was an excellent doctor who could cure almost anything and taught her golden rule: "A doctor's duty is to treat whatever ailments they can." She also taught that some illnesses are incurable, and that sometimes you trick a child into taking medicine. Her teacher's body was never found. Sigewinne built a simple cenotaph by the water in what is now the Morte Region; rising water has since swallowed it.

She left Sigewinne a riddle: if all humans die, why do humans exist? Sigewinne's answer, "for their smiles and tears", came only years later, after Oldstone. The witch had discovered a disease that dissolves human bodies into water, which she suspected every Fontainian carried. She experimented on herself until her condition was fatal. On her last night she made a final gamble to cure it and told Sigewinne to come back in two hours, or not to look for her if it failed. It failed. She left behind a bottle and a note.

After the flood exposed the truth about the Oceanids, Sigewinne opened the letter her teacher had sealed in a bottle. Her teacher apologised for lying "even at the end": the liquid left by a dissolved body, mixed with certain ingredients, made a face-changing solution only Fontainians could use. The bottle had held her own dissolved body. Sigewinne says it was exactly the sort of thing her teacher would do. She feels the "warmth" of that lie whenever she touches her cheeks. She thanked her and laid the letter on the water to drift away.

3.content:
In the times when humans and Melusines did not trust each other, only one little girl befriended Sigewinne; they liked to play doctor and patient. When the girl fell gravely ill, her parents turned Sigewinne away because she was a Melusine. Sigewinne went to her teacher, swore she would bear any cost as long as she hurt no one, and took the potion left for her. It gave her a human face, hands and feet, and she cured the girl. The change broke an ancient Fontainian law against forcibly changing a species into human form. She confessed to Neuvillette herself, and after confirming the facts he gave his verdict: the Fortress of Meropide.

The Iudex let her keep her medical kit. In the Fortress no one refused her treatment, and every patient she treated shortened her sentence, until the Fortress could not do without her. Her sentence ended and she stayed. Later she received an invitation from an old woman: the girl she had saved, fifty years on. The old woman said that everyone could tell Sigewinne was not human, since she had not aged a day. She had recognised her by the warmth of her palm, unchanged, and thanked her as "Doctor Melusine".

Sigewinne thinks her conviction was fair, not unfair. Serving it, she says, is what let her stay strong when Potton insisted they were the same. In 4.7, with permission from the Marechaussee Phantom, she brewed a few bottles of the potion to restore the face-swapping victims. She offered a spare to the Traveler and Paimon, declined to use it to regain her old form, and destroyed it with them.

4.comment: Sigewinne: The Fortress infirmary and its unwritten rules
4.content:
Sigewinne's infirmary is one of the few places in the Fortress open to everyone at all hours. Guards and inmates wake to find a hot drink, a clean bed or their lunch waiting. She has taken very few days off during Wriothesley's tenure, and the lights never go out. One inmate saw the wings on her back and called her an emissary of the heavens. Soon most of the Fortress agreed she was their angel and their "sun". The guards keep an unwritten rule that anyone rude to her is punished extra harshly, and the inmates "warn" violent newcomers on arrival. She knows none of this.

Early in her time as head nurse she decided exhaustion was an illness, since so many inmates overworked themselves for Credit Coupons, and invented a cure. Her first patient blanched at it. The inmate who served as head chef agreed to cook it, provided no one ever saw her bring the ingredients; today Wolsey prepares it for her. As the "Nutritious Meal", it turns up on the tray of anyone who overworked the day before. Its recipe includes slime condensate, xenochromatic crystals and frog meat. Her official introduction mentions a long-standing agreement among all who live in the Fortress not to harm its medical staff, and a rumour that she founded the infirmary.

She invites Marechaussee Phantom Melusines for tea in the infirmary, but does not want them working there long unless they switch to medicine, since inmates sent down by the Phantom may not want to see uniformed Melusines. Pankration fighters who cry at injections get candy and stickers. Her storeroom keeps filling with mechanical parts, for reasons she has not explained, and she wants the Duke to enlarge it.

5.content:
Sigewinne is a Melusine: born of the dragon Elynas, long-lived, and Neuvillette's familiar. When Melusines first came onto land, people feared them as Elynas's offspring, distrusted them because they distrusted Neuvillette, or recoiled because they looked different. Most retreated to the water. Sigewinne stayed out of curiosity. To Melusines, human ageing and death are as natural as sunrise and sunset. Unlike most of her kind, she came to understand death and incurable illness. Melusines perceive the world differently and judge people by "cuteness", and she is no exception.

Her closest Melusine friends are Ottnit and Menthe. When work is quiet they drink tea in the infirmary, discuss criminal cases and skincare, and mostly paint cute things to turn into stickers for cute people. Long ago, Neuvillette banned Melusines from giving gifts to humans after bad actors exploited that kindness. The Melusine officer who fed the starving young Wriothesley did so only on his express instructions.

6.content:
The Traveler met Sigewinne when Wriothesley showed them around the Fortress; over a meal at the Coupon Cafeteria she decided they were cute. When they worked two days straight in the Production Zone, her special meal arrived. To probe the infirmary for Lyney, the Traveler faked illness. She examined them thoroughly, diagnosed a mild upset stomach, prescribed medicine, rest and bland food, and played along, knowing all the while. She later shared dinner with them and Clorinde, explained how she reads expressions, and asked them to stay longer because their smiles were contagious. She escorted them to the surface when their "sentence" ended.

In The Warmth of Lies she had the Traveler fake illness again, this time to persuade a boy, Luc, to drink bitter medicine. Paimon bluntly asked if she was half-Melusine; the Traveler disapproved, and Sigewinne answered with her story. She trusted them with her teacher's secret, took them to the memorial and kept her promise of a potion, which they destroyed together. Her birthday letters invite the Traveler for a check-up and ask them to promise to rest.

7.comment: Sigewinne: The House of the Hearth siblings in the Fortress
7.content:
During the 4.1 Archon Quest the House of the Hearth siblings infiltrated the Fortress. Lynette was sedated in an empty room during a confrontation, and Sigewinne and Wriothesley left her tea and snacks. When Lyney lunged at Wriothesley in his office, Sigewinne stopped him with a tranquilizer dart. She called it the least harmful option and still apologises for it. Clorinde then brought in Freminet, unconscious after Primordial Seawater got into his diving gear. Sigewinne diagnosed acute ingestion from a flushed face and racing pulse, reassured Lyney it was not critical, and treated him in the infirmary.

She had asked Wriothesley to keep an eye on "that diver boy" when the water seemed wrong. She also kept watch on Lyney so that, pressed as he was, he would never be in real danger. Freminet later came to thank her and was absorbed in the Melusines' paintings; she thinks he has a rich inner world. Lynette is "human-being-cute and kitty-cute", and Sigewinne would love to pat her head, with permission.

8.comment: Sigewinne: The Warmth of Lies and the Butterfly Dew case
8.content:
Her story quest (4.7). Wriothesley sent her on vacation, and in the Court of Fontaine she and the Traveler met "Rawat" of the Fontaine Research Institute, selling a skin lotion, Butterfly Dew. She praised it to his face but privately judged it in need of refinement. Back in the Fortress, inmates reported seeing their doppelgangers, and some serious offenders swapped faces with inmates due for release and walked out. With the Duke's approval she joined the Marechaussee Phantom's investigation. She treated a sick old woman at Rawat's registered address and found a map to a secret factory. There Potton, the man behind "Rawat", sealed them in and released poison gas. She bargained with a better formula that needs no Primordial Water, and had already prepared an antidote.

The lotion and the face-changing potion were made from the remains of Fontainians who had dissolved in Primordial Seawater. Since Neuvillette absolved Fontainians of their sin, the faces of those who used them began to "melt". Potton had been rejected all his life for his face and remade himself as handsome "Rawat". He argued that Sigewinne had done exactly what he did. She persuaded Morgane to let him see his dying mother one last time, but his mother no longer recognised him; she recognised Sigewinne instead. Sigewinne felt the warmth leave his hand and said the roots of his problem were never his face. Afterwards she promised the Marechaussee Phantom to keep the potion secret.

9.content: An old inmate known only as "Oldstone" refused treatment for years, and when guards finally dragged him in, his illness proved terminal. Sigewinne felt trapped for the first time. Then she noticed him staring at one date on the calendar. Remembering her teacher, she offered to treat the one ailment she could: his inability to last until that day. He drank every bitter concoction for ten days and lived past his prognosis. On the day, a mother and her son, the son he had failed as a father and a merchant back from Liyue, came to reconcile with him before he died. Among the family's thank-you gifts she found a brand-new Hydro Vision. She took it as one more note on her answer: medicine exists "for the smiles and tears on their faces".

10.content: Clorinde stayed in the Fortress as a guest after rescuing Freminet from the sea, and Sigewinne took her for a check-up and made her dinner. Sigewinne finds her face hard to read. She gave Clorinde a lipstick and was delighted to hear she uses it. Clorinde calls her an excellent nurse, equally good at treating the injured and comforting the distressed. She thinks Sigewinne's kindness may bring out what little good there is in the Fortress's worst offenders.

11.comment: Sigewinne: Beauty columns and the Fontaine Beauty Association
11.content:
Sigewinne writes skincare and beauty columns for the magazine Beautes en fleurs under the pen name "Romaritime Flower". She also attends the Fontaine Beauty Association's regular meetings. Most readers' letters lament their looks; she writes to help people care for and love the faces they have, and holds that no one has the right to judge or compare others' appearance. Navia accepts compliments joyfully and takes photos with her. Emilie's perfumes are recommended everywhere, and Sigewinne plans to cut her next vacation visit to the Palais Mermonia short so she can buy armfuls of them for the girls back in the Fortress. A Vasari Passage notice says she will host a beauty lecture.

She loves Charlotte's photographs for the facial muscles they capture. Chiori's Melusine tailoring lets her friends wear the clothes they love. She makes her own creams and compresses with Tidalga extract and once gave the Traveler a portable skincare set for their birthday. Asked whether a cream reverses ageing, she says no product can, and suggests reporting anyone who claims otherwise to the Gardes.

12.comment: Sigewinne: Furina's trial and the flood
12.content: When the Fortress's sluice gates broke and Neuvillette came to hold back the water, Sigewinne treated the injured and asked the Traveler to stay a few days. At Furina's trial she examined the Hydro Archon after Furina dipped her hands in Primordial Water. She reported flushed skin and hyperventilation, the same reaction as any other Fontainian at that concentration. After the flood she settled the injured inmates, then went back to the Fortress early to open her teacher's sealed letter. At the celebration afterwards she offered everyone a new drink.

13.content: In Neuvillette's story quest, someone in the Fortress put out a hit on the Melusine Kiara, and the Iudex came down to investigate in person. Hearing the word "Melusine", Sigewinne rushed over to ask whether Kiara would be alright. She settled the visitors in the infirmary with tea, reminding them that thirst means you are already dehydrated. She then brought Neuvillette word that Wriothesley had found the suspect, Domenico, and later took Domenico back to his cell.

14.content: Escoffier spent a short time in the Fortress. Whenever Sigewinne made her a drink, she took tiny, serious sips and analysed the flavour in detail, which Sigewinne found adorable. Sigewinne wants to send her more milkshakes. Escoffier calls the head nurse lovely but her taste "unique". She tried to understand the flavours from a Melusine's point of view and concluded the milkshakes are "absolutely deadly".

15.comment: Sigewinne: Lantern Rite with the Duke (6.3 event)
15.content: During a limited-time Lantern Rite event in Liyue (6.3), the Traveler found Sigewinne at the festival. Wriothesley had invited her to experience Lantern Rite, and to finally use up the vacation days she had never taken. A kind lady at the harbour had promised them a professional photographer, who turned out to be the Traveler. Sigewinne posed for a keepsake to show Neuvillette. She also released a Xiao Lantern for a former Fortress patient who had wished to release one himself.

16.comment: Sigewinne: The aquarium and the irate fish (6.7 event)
16.content: During the limited-time Sunny Summer Fontinalia event (6.7), the Traveler ran an aquarium aboard the docked Wingalet. "Miss Guillotin" invited Sigewinne as marine consultant; she had picked up animal care looking after the animals at Chevalmarin Film Fantasyland. Wild fish had been attacking divers and boats, so she treated them as inpatients: aquarium rest and Melusine herbal medicine in the tanks. She traced the aggression to shipwrecks and illegally dumped junk wrecking their habitats, pushed the cleanup divers to hurry, gathered sensor data, and filed an incident report with the Palais Mermonia so regulations could be drafted. She hoped a film might one day teach people to protect the water, and loved Paimon's idea of a monster movie about it.

17.content: In a 7.1 anecdote in Snezhnograd, the dancer Odette is eating a strict, healthy diet that Sigewinne designed for her. They met at a cafe after a show, when Odette was in Fontaine to pick up a custom outfit, and Odette asked her about nutrition. The diet includes cheat days. Odette found a meal Sigewinne made herself "perfectly edible". Her friend Vodyanitsa got in touch with Sigewinne through opera contacts in Fontaine and asked about a healthy dessert. Sigewinne replied that dessert now and then is fine, was glad Odette was doing well, and asked that she be told not to be so hard on herself: mental and physical health go hand in hand. Sigewinne does not appear on-screen.
